text:
alex.k: heads up — ACME reported a mismatch between their reserved GPU invoice for Feb and what our dashboard shows. Invoice billed 840 reserved hours; dashboard shows 560 used. Customer is upset, escalated by CSM.

maria_s: account id? billing period? any tenant IDs?

alex.k: acct_acme_01, billing period 2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-28. CSM said they pin to dedicated pool rp-dedicated-eu and didn't change anything.

samir: is this the same issue as last month where burst routing created duplicate hour attributions? asking because 840 vs 560 is a 50% delta.

jess: attaching billing export they sent. Also they attached hourly CSV with two columns: dashboard_reserved_hours and invoice_billed_hours.

alex.k: pasted snippet they sent:

```
hour, dashboard_reserved_hours, invoice_hours
2026-02-02T01:00Z, 8, 12
2026-02-02T02:00Z, 4, 6
... 
total, 560, 840
```

maria_s: thanks. can billing team run the internal meter report for acct_acme_01 for feb and include breakdown by routing tag (reserved_vs_burst) and instance_id?

billing-bot: /billing run-report --account=acct_acme_01 --from=2026-02-01 --to=2026-02-28 --granularity=hour --tags=reserved,burst --output=json

billing-bot: Report queued (job id jb_98321). ETA ~ 90s.

oncall-sre: tagging in case it's an inference runtime double-counting bug; last release to routing gateway was 2026-02-15.

samir: quick hypothesis: if a request was routed to a dedicated server but then retried and routed to hosted fallback, both attempts might have been flagged as 'reserved' on the dedicated meter and also as 'burst' on the hosted meter. That could double-count hours if post-processing script sums both without dedup.

jess: customer claims they didn't see increased application errors or retries. They did see a transient SLA fallback event on 2026-02-15 at 03:14Z (reported).

alex.k: pasted customer's observability note: "2026-02-15 03:14Z — request latencies spiked, retried client-side, some calls returned 503 then succeeded on second attempt."

maria_s: can ops pull the routing logs for that 03:14Z window. Need request ids and final routing decision. Also we should correlate with meter events for both dedicated and hosted pools.

billing-bot: job jb_98321 completed. summary:
```
- reserved_pool_hours: 560
- burst_pool_hours: 120
- duplicate_counted_attempts: 160
- invoice_total_hours: 840
```

samir: billing bot shows duplicate_counted_attempts=160 — that exactly accounts for 280 extra hours? Wait math: 560 + 120 = 680; invoice 840 -> diff 160. That maps.

jess: so looks like the meter flagged 160 hours as both reserved and invoice included them separately. Need to trace why duplicate_counted_attempts occurred.

oncall-sre: pulled routing logs for 2026-02-15 03:12-03:18Z. Found many requests with header `x-rw-routing: reserved:rp-dedicated-eu` then client retries with same request id and routed to hosted fallback `rw-hosted-us-east`. We have entries where both attempts logged the same logical request_id but unique attempt ids.

maria_s: crucial question — does billing aggregation deduplicate by logical request_id or by attempt id?

billing-bot: current billing aggregation deduplicates by attempt id only. This was intentional historically but causes double billing across pools when attempts cross pool boundaries.

alex.k: so policy is to bill every attempt unless it's explicitly flagged as retry? that seems bad for retries that end up succeeding.

samir: agreed. For dedicated customers we should prefer to bill the successful reserved attempt if it hit reserved pool first, or at least dedupe by original request_id for the same time window.

jess: quick mitigation for ACME: credit them for the duplicate 160 hours and file a follow-up to change dedupe logic. Customer expectation is they only pay for final successful execution or a single attempt.

cs_lead: agree — issue a credit and explain root cause. Also offer temporary override: cap billed reserved hours to dashboard_reserved_hours while we fix pipeline.

maria_s: ops/infra follow-up: change needed in billing pipeline — when aggregating meter events, dedupe on `original_request_id` across pools and mark attempt_type (success/failure). If original_request_id not present, fall back to attempt id. Also we need a migration to backfill feb invoices for impacted accounts.

oncall-sre: opened issue INFRA-3412 with logs + sample request ids. Added suspected release that introduced the header rename `x-rw-request-id` -> `x-rw-original-id` on 2026-02-15 which caused older components to generate new ids. That broke dedupe.

samir: timeline: 1) Issue confirmed, causes double-counting when ID renaming occurred. 2) Short-term: issue credits to affected customers and add billing cap for dedicated customers. 3) Medium-term: update billing dedupe to prefer original_request_id, and ensure routing preserves original id on retries. 4) Long-term: add end-to-end test and alert on sudden invoice vs dashboard deltas > 10%.

alex.k: customer response: "Thanks. We appreciate the quick credit and the plan. Please confirm when invoice adjustment posted."

jess: action items assigned:
- billing: prepare credit for acct_acme_01 (jess)
- infra: ensure routing preserves original_request_id across retries (samir)
- billing pipeline: change dedupe logic + run backfill job for Feb (billing-bot)
- cs: communicate to ACME and confirm when adjustment posted (cs_lead)

billing-bot: created ticket BILL-7724 (dedupe change) and BACKFILL-2201 (feb adjustments). ETA for code fix: 5 business days. Backfill ETA: 3 business days after code is in prod.

maria_s: thumbs up. please update this thread with PR links and when credits hit invoices. Also add postmortem after backfill completes.

cs_lead: I will send ACME a short explanation + expected timeline now.

alex.k: thanks all. will close once backfill done and ACME confirms. :thumbsup:
